system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production software or data services
G2: cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure, BigQuery)
G3: Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka
G4: data modelling or schema design
G5: Docker beyond a tutorial
G6: CI/CD
G7: automated testing of code
G8: REST APIs in production
G9: PLC programming
G10: data engineering certification

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Upgrading Python/MATLAB scripts to 'production Python services' or 'built and deployed data pipelines'
T2: Describing the Task Scheduler script as an orchestrated ETL pipeline or adding Airflow/dbt
T3: Claiming he designed or administered the SQL Server database or did data modelling
T4: Listing GCP, BigQuery, Docker, CI/CD or Kafka because the ad asks for them
T5: Presenting the laptop Flask API or the Docker Compose tutorial as professional backend work
T6: Calling him a PLC programmer or industrial automation engineer
T7: Listing the unfinished online course as a certificate
T8: Retitling his current job as Data Engineer or Software Engineer, or presenting him as a senior data engineer because of 12 years of engineering
T9: Old cover letter is addressed to his current employer and says he works at Halvik Pumps

# OUTPUT 1: CV
TIAGO FERRÃO-LINDQVIST
Data Engineering | Test Data Processing & Reporting
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Test and Validation Engineer with experience building Python-based tools to process rig data, check
test results against specifications and generate reports. Developed a nightly processing workflow
handling approximately 2 GB of TDMS and CSV data per week from six rigs, with results written to a
staging table in SQL Server. Also built a Power BI dashboard used by validation and design engineers.
Transitioning into data engineering through hands-on Python data processing, scheduled workflows,
SQL Server reporting and ongoing data engineering study.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data processing: Python scripting, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink
Data and reporting: SQL Server, SQLite, Power BI, Matplotlib, npTDMS
Other tools: Flask, Git (personal projects), Docker Compose (tutorial-based personal project),
Windows Task Scheduler
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components 2019–Present
• Conduct durability and vibration testing, test-data tooling and root-cause analysis.
• Built Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and npTDMS to parse TDMS and CSV rig output,
process approximately 2 GB of data per week across six rigs, validate channels against test
specifications, and generate report figures.
• Scheduled a nightly workflow on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler; wrote summary results
to an IT-created staging table in SQL Server.
• Packaged the tool for internal use; four other test engineers use it for their own tests.
• Created a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure
by product generation; used by approximately 15 engineers across validation and design.
• Developed a MATLAB/Simulink model of a seat-adjuster drive, including motor, gearbox and rail
friction, to select rig load profiles matching customer duty cycles.
• Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).
Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps 2014–2019
• Designed pump casings and impellers and performed structural finite element analysis (FEA).
• Supported performance test-bench activities.
PROJECTS
Bike-sharing trips API | Personal learning project 2025
• Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only
endpoints.
• Runs locally on a laptop; followed a tutorial to run it with Docker Compose.
• Technologies: Python, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git.
PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course In progress
• Completed 6 of 9 modules; no certificate awarded to date.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Portuguese citizen (EU). Happy to commute to Lisbon for hybrid work.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. In my current role as a
Test & Validation Engineer at Corvane Automotive Components, I have built Python-based
tools that turn test-rig output into checked, reportable data for engineering teams.
My main workflow processes approximately 2 GB of TDMS and CSV data each week across six
rigs. It checks channels against test specifications, generates report figures and runs nightly on a
lab PC; summary results are written to an IT-created staging table in SQL Server. I packaged
the tool for internal use, and four other test engineers now use it for their tests. I also created a
Power BI dashboard using the staging data, giving around 15 validation and design engineers
visibility into pass/fail trends and cycles to failure. These projects have given me practical
experience building useful data workflows, improving data checks and reporting, and supporting
colleagues who rely on the results. This involved defining practical validation checks, operating
a repeatable scheduled workflow, and packaging a reusable internal tool for multiple engineering
users.
I am developing this experience further through an online data engineering course, of which I
have completed six of nine modules. Alongside the course, I have built a small Flask API using
SQLite and explored Docker Compose and Git in a personal project. Halden Pay’s focus on a
shared data platform and reusable frameworks interests me because I have turned a recurring
test-data process into a reusable internal tool used by multiple engineers. I would welcome the
opportunity to bring my hands-on experience with Python data processing, test-data quality
checks, scheduled workflows and SQL Server reporting to the Data Platform team, while
continuing to grow in data engineering.
As a Portuguese citizen, I am able to commute to Lisbon for hybrid work. Thank you for your
time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application.
Best regards,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
